result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers commit to refining the logo and base that on the twelve years of recognition and the move to three locations. B gives a designer more to work with: a heavier small version for 16–32 px, one line weight that keeps some irregularity, location names on a separate line, and checks in black and reversed. B also answers the partner with concrete tests and clear grounds for replacing the logo, while A relies mainly on a side-by-side mockup. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers choose to refine, base that choice on twelve years of local recognition and the move to three locations, and give a designer clear, usable steps, including a system of layout versions with each location's name set below the mark. A is a bit stronger on how the mark works in practice, with a separate heavier small version and a black-at-16px test. B is a bit stronger on the clinic's situation and on winning over the partner: it points out that the risk is greatest just as the new sites open, proposes side-by-side mockups and a 'same dog, fresh look' rollout, and suggests protecting the details the owner loves.
